test_title: PYST 25: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - English Language (Held On 28 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The professor's explanation (1)/ was filled in clarity (2)/ yet managed to obfuscate (3)/ more than elucidate. (4)
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary error in the sentence is the use of the incorrect preposition "**in**" after the word "**filled**" in **part 2**.
 
• In English, the standard phrasal verb to indicate that something is full of a particular quality or substance is "**filled with**."
 
• "**Filled in**" is typically used in the context of completing a form or a hole (e.g., "fill in the blanks").
 
• To maintain grammatical accuracy, "**filled in clarity**" must be changed to "**filled with clarity**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The professor's explanation was **filled with clarity** yet managed to obfuscate more than elucidate."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **(1) "The professor's explanation"** – This is the subject of the sentence and is grammatically correct.
 
• **(3) "yet managed to obfuscate"** – "Yet" is a conjunction showing contrast, and "obfuscate" (meaning to make obscure or unclear) is used correctly as an infinitive.
 
• **(4) "more than elucidate."** – "Elucidate" means to make something clear; this part correctly completes the comparison started in part 3.
 
• **Note:** While the sentence contains a semantic paradox (an explanation filled with clarity shouldn't obfuscate), the specific grammatical error is the prepositional usage in part 2.
